hypothesis: Replace the FM's pointwise BCE training objective with a BPR-style pairwise logistic loss — for each positive training row, sample one negative row from the *same user* (vectorized via precomputed per-user negative-index ranges, no python-level per-row loop, so it stays cheap), and train on -log(sigmoid(score_pos - score_neg)) instead of binary cross-entropy on individual rows. Per the literature note found via last iteration's web-research question ("BPR Pairwise Loss for Optimizing GAUC/nDCG in Implicit-Feedback Ranking"), this directly aligns the training signal with GAUC's actual definition (fraction of correctly-ordered pos/neg pairs per user) rather than optimizing an unrelated pointwise probability calibration objective.
reflection: My last iteration used the web-research call and found that BPR-style pairwise loss is a well-established, practical fit for optimizing GAUC/nDCG-style rank metrics in an FM model without expensive per-user negative sampling (it can be done with vectorized in-batch/per-user negative sampling). Given I already have this specific, actionable finding in hand, spending another research call now would be wasteful — the higher-leverage move is to actually implement it, since it's a genuinely different mechanism (training objective) from the two failed feature-engineering attempts that caused the plateau, and it directly targets GAUC (which literally *is* a per-user pairwise-ranking accuracy metric) in a way pointwise BCE never explicitly optimizes for.
expected_effect: GAUC should move more than nDCG@5, since BPR's pairwise objective is a near-exact training-time surrogate for per-user AUC (GAUC), whereas nDCG@5's within-user top-k emphasis is only indirectly helped by uniform pairwise ranking.
